headline: Postponed approval of August minutes; discussed energy grants, EV charging, and the community choice aggregation program.
summary: Katrin Kasper of Clean Energy NH explained how the group helps communities with solar, efficiency, and EV charging projects. Kasper said most available grant money requires projects to be shovel ready. Town hall resource limits will likely delay staff review of the SolarAPP+ permitting app.
decisions: Postponed approval of the August 4, 2026 meeting minutes to the next subcommittee meeting.

decision_evidence.quote: Approval of August 4, 2026 meeting minutes postponed to the next subcommittee meeting.

plain_text:
LONDONDERRY UTILITIES COMMITTEE 
ENERGY SUBCOMMITTEE  
MEETING MINUTES 
4:00 PM Tuesday, September 22, 2026 
Sunnycrest Conference Room - Londonderry Town Hall 
 
I. Called to Order at 3:59 PM.  
II. Attendees- Lynn Wiles, Mike Speltz, James Danis, John Mahon, Martha Smith, Paul Ramsey, 
Joy Muller, and Katrin Kasper from Clean Energy NH 
III. Public Comment- None 
IV. Subcommittee Administrative Work 
a. Approval of August 4, 2026 meeting minutes postponed to the next subcommittee 
meeting. 
V. New Business 
a. Katrin Kasper, Clean Energy NH. Katrin briefed the subcommittee on how Clean Energy 
NH works with communities across the state to implement energy related projects 
including solar, energy efficiency, and EV charging infrastructure. 
b. Clean Energy NH will work with the subcommittee to set up a community-wide listening 
session to solicit ideas and receive feedback on energy related projects. Kasper 
reiterated that most grant money available requires that projects be shovel ready.  
c. Lynn Wiles will forward a copy of Londonderry’s Solar zoning ordinance to Clean Energy 
NH for their review and feedback.  
d. Kasper will work with James Danis to investigate NH Saves funds that could be applied 
to the Town Hall renovations currently underway. 
e. Discussion on the “Recharge the Adventure New Hampshire” grant program designed to 
expand the EV charging station infrastructure in the state to better support tourism and 
economic development. 
f. Clean Energy NH is holding its annual Local Energy Solutions Conference on November 
22, location TBA. Londonderry receives four tickets to the conference as part of its 
membership.
VI. Old Business 
a. Community Choice Aggregation Program- Lynn Wiles gave a presentation on the status 
of the program to the Town Council on September 21. The presentation was very well 
received.  
b. Continued discussion on implementing the SolarAPP+ permitting tool. Town hall 
resource constraints will likely delay staff review of the app. 
VII. Round Table Discussion 
VIII. Public Comment- None 
IX. Next Meeting- December 1, 2026 
X. Meeting Adjournment at 5:45 PM.
